lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: That’s the one--

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Um, yeah, you’re singing this with me.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Hey, this is my night. I’m a lawyer now. I’ve been barred a whole... Three hours. So I can sue you if you don’t sing with me.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Yeah? I’ll double sue you.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: It could be, once my full power is unleashed. You willing to take that risk?

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Wow, Ernie’s really going for it.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Uh-oh. Chuck’s gonna bail.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: The guy never has any fun. I was hoping he would, y’know... “mingle” with some of the ladyfolk...

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Okay, I’m goin’ in.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Pick us a good song! Not this decade!

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Hey, buddy. You’re not leaving already, are ya?

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: C’mon! Ten minutes. You can do ten more. Ten! That’s nothing--

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: You can’t go. My song’s up next! Stay. C’mon, look... If you go and everyone at work tomorrow is talking about my performance, you’re never gonna forgive yourself for missing it.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Great! You won’t regret it--

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Oh, that’s me!

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I don't want to talk, About the things we've gone through, Though it's hurting me, Now it's history.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Chuck! Come on up here!

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I've played all my cards, And that's what you've done too... Chuck McGill everyone! Let’s hear it!

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: No more ace to play... The winner takes it all!

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: There ya go!

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Beside the victory, That's her destiny... I was in your arms...

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I figured it made sense, Building me a fence...

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: McGill and McGill. The brothers McGill. I’m a lawyer... and you’re a lawyer. How ‘bout that? Two lawyers. M & M. Melts in your mouth, not in your hands.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Hey, you should talk to Howard about adding another “M” to the firm. It’s more symmetrical. People love symmetricality.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: That’s why God gave everybody two eyes. It’s pleasing to look at. Two hands. Two feet. Thumbs. Two nipples. We could all get along fine with just the one nipple, but, c’mon. Two is obviously better. Am I right?

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Thank you. Four or six nipples... that’s interesting, but, ultimately, I submit to the court, overkill.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: H-H-M-M. “Hmmmmmmm.” See, that’s just better. Otherwise, it’s only, “Hmph.” You should be writing this down--

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: You... you think of everything. So smart.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Thank you. Thank you, Chuck. You’re the best.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Oh, pancakes. Make those pancakes you make.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: It was. It was a big day. Good night, Chuck.

lines.scene: INT. KARAOKE BAR - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: The winner takes it all...

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Watermelon, pickles... Watermelon, pickles... Watermelon, pickles...

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: One one thousand, two one thousand, three one thousand, four one thousand, five--

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Oh. Hi. It’s so nice of you to visit.

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: That’s right. Jimmy.

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Oh, sure. I remember. He spoke fondly of you both.

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: But... you came today, so...

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: I know. It still doesn’t make any sense.

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: And bless you. Very thoughtful.

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: No. Coffee. And gimme one of those bear claws.

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Well, good sign we got customers this early, right? Wasn’t sure anyone was gonna come. mourners) How’d it look?

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: It felt like I looked sad.

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Howard picked a big one. Very tasteful.

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Oh. I know that car. It’s Judge Padilla. Padilla loved Chuck.

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Gotta get back.

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Should I try for tears this time?

lines.scene: EXT. CEMETERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yeah. Maybe best not to force it.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Twenty-three thousand dollars. I can't believe I wrote a twenty- three thousand dollar check for this. You know how many phones I had to sell to make that money?

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: For a plaque. It’s not like they had to build anything -- the room was already there! "Naming rights." What a rip-off. Kim, I just don't think it's bang for the buck. I don’t see anyone in there from the bar association.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: “Word gets around.” I get it. But I just think... We can do more.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Picture this: Judge Papadoumian is in her chambers. She’s working late. Everyone's gone home.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: She smells something... What is that? Could it be... something burning? She goes to the door, it's warm to the touch. She opens it -- her clerk's chambers are a wall of flames! She's trapped. But then... what's this? Through the fire and smoke, a figure emerges -- it's Jimmy McGill! Listen, I rescue a judge? That people are gonna talk about...

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yeah. I know. That’s not how I come back from “insincere.”

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: I’m starving. Those little hamburgers are lookin’ pretty good. I know, I know. I can pay for the food but I can’t eat the food. Why can’t sad people eat?

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: The one vote for Kristy Esposito? That's me. JJIIMMMMYY ((CCOONNTT''DD)) And, for what it’s worth, I think we should give her another look.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: The shoplifter. That's right. Her grades are good -- maybe not quite as good as some of these other kids, but good. Her recommendations are solid. And, yes, she had some trouble. She was new in town and she made some bad choices. But that was sophomore year, she's had two really strong years since then.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: And her essay? I hope everyone read this. Turns out the experience got her interested in the law. It’s good, it’s really good.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: My point is this. Maybe someone who's been in trouble, maybe someone who doesn't have a perfect record -- someone who’s made mistakes and faced the consequences -- maybe she brings something the others don't. She's been tested and she came out of it. I think she deserves real consideration.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Kristy! Ms. Esposito! Wait up!

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Hi... I’m Jimmy McGill, we met inside.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: You didn't get it.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Let me tell you something. You were never gonna get it. They dangle these things in front of you, they tell you you've got a chance -- but it's a lie. 'Cause they already made up their minds. JJIIMMMMYY ((CCOONNTT''DD)) They knew what they were going to do before you walked in the door. You made a mistake and they’re not forgetting it, not ever. Far as they’re concerned, your mistake is who you are. It's all you are.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: I’m not just talking about this scholarship -- I’m talking about everything. Look, I read your essay. You can do it the way you’re supposed to, you can work fifty times harder than the rest of them. Makes no difference. They’ll smile at you, they’ll pat you on the head -- but they’re never, ever gonna let you in.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: But listen. It doesn't matter. You don't need them. They're not gonna give it to you? So what! You're gonna take it.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: You’re gonna do whatever it takes. You’re not gonna play by their rules. You’re not even gonna try. Go the other way. Do what they won’t. Be smarter. Cut corners. And win. They’re on the thirty- fifth floor? So what! You’re on the fiftieth floor looking down on them. The higher you climb, the more they’re gonna hate you. Good. Rub their noses in it. Make ‘em suffer. You don’t matter all that much to them? Then screw them.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Winner takes it all.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Do you understand what I’m saying to you?

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Damn right you do. Go get ‘em.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Winner takes it all.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Come on. Damnit.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Damn. No. No. No.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: God... damn it!

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Hey.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yeah.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: We gave scholarships to three very bright young people.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yeah.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: How do we know for sure?

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: I can say whatever I want. To the board I’m still Jimmy McGill.

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: What if... What if...

lines.scene: INT. UNIVERSITY LIBRARY - HALL - DAY
lines.dialogue: What if Chuck does the talking for me?

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: This should do it. Chuck wrote a good letter, right?

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: Thank you, your Honor. I, um... I actually don’t have a prepared statement, but I do have this... JJIIMMMMYY ((CCOONNTT''DD)) It’s a letter my brother, Charles McGill, wrote and, uh... he left it to me in his will, which I received after he passed last year.

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: “I left many things unsaid in our relationship through the years. Rather than allow these unspoken thoughts to die with me, I’ve chosen to record them here for you. I hope you will take my words in the spirit in which they are intended.”

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: “I remember quite clearly the day you came home from the hospital. You can’t imagine...”

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: “Can’t imagine the joy on mom’s face...”

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: I... I can’t do this.

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: I’m sorry.

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: You know, I, uh... I was gonna move you all with my brother’s eloquent words about me. Really pull on those heartstrings. But, uh... that... JJIIMMMMYY ((CCOONNTT''DD)) It’s not right. It’s not. This letter’s between me and him. And it should stay that way.

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: Besides, he didn’t write this to me when I was a lawyer, so... Look, my brother loved me, in his own way. Loved me as a brother, but... He did not love me as a lawyer.

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: Big part of the reason I became a lawyer was... Chuck. He was the most brilliant man I ever knew. An incredible lawyer. And he knew exactly who he was. Exactly. And I wanted to make him proud. And, believe me, he was a hard man to make proud. Like climbing Everest without supplies. But if you were one of the few who reached the peak, made him proud even for a moment... Wow. What a feeling. He let you know it. But if you weren’t one of those people...

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: He was always polite enough to everyone, but he sure didn’t suffer fools, y’know? He was judgmental. He was difficult. Knew how to get under your skin. And he could be a real son-of-a-bitch. Chuck was the one who was “always right.” Always. JJIIMMMMYY ((CCOONNTT''DD)) And, honestly, he usually was. So, y’know, a guy like me... did lousy in school, lacked ambition, always cut corners... For me to live up to somebody like Charles McGill... heh, c’mon. Look at me. I’ll never be as moral as him. Never be as smart. Never as respected. I’ll never be as good as Chuck. But I can try. I can try. And if

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: I’m still going to be the best man I can be.

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: Look, I’m lucky. I got this letter.

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: I never wrote a letter to him. Never got a chance to say all the things I should’ve. I gotta believe, somehow, he knows...

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: I’m sorry. That’s... That’ll have to do it for me. I-- Thank you.

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: That felt... so good.

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: Uh, yeah! God, didja see those suckers? I had them! And that one asshole at the end was actually crying? He had tears. Jesus...

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: I mean, I started reading the letter, but I could just tell, I could see it on their faces it wasn’t gonna be enough, so I just kinda went off on this... flow. This energy going through me, like it was improv, or jazz!

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: Then I just -- pop -- sank the hook in. I had ‘em, like a pied piper leading the rats right into the river. Y’know, I could see it, I could see the Matrix. Like I was invincible. I mean, God... I can dodge bullets, baby.

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: And Kim, you were right, you were so right. It was all about Chuck!

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: Oh, I know. Believe me...

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: Ab-so-lutely. Let’s do this thing! Oh, sweetheart, I’m gonna need one more form. A DBA. Turns out I won’t be practicing under the name McGill.

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: Great!

lines.scene: EXT. DULCE VEGA HOT SPRINGS HOTEL & SPA - FRONT AREA - DAY
lines.dialogue: S’all good, man.
raspy) Yeah. It’s me. JJIIMMMMYY ((OO..SS..)) ((CCOONNTT''DD)) I’m okay.
Let's do it.
De Guzman. Jorge.
Yep.
It's not for me to ask where a client gets his money.
Jorge de Guzman.
And now... Mr. De Guzman?
Car trouble. Broke down about six miles from the pick-up site. Y'know there's no cell reception out there, right?
Yeah. Just... kaput.

I thought of that, yeah. But with seven million in cash... I was afraid who might pick me up. I didn't think it was worth the risk. I went north. Maybe not the smartest idea, but... after a night lost in the desert, I made it.
Ahhh-ahhhhh--
Anyway, look... I wouldn't be too happy, yet. That seven million, it sent up a huge flare. They're looking into you. I don't know how long "Jorge de Guzman" is gonna hold up.
Right.
My... my what?
I’m okay, I’m okay... I-- I washed it out good at the truck stop--
I don’t need an IV. I’ve been pounding down sports drinks nonstop. I, really, I’m okay...
What is this, Cream of Wheat?
Ahh, yeah. It’s good.
Yeah.
I’m good. I’m just gonna... sit. This is good.
That's right. All by myself.
So... Anything you wanna tell me?
Lalo. You saw Lalo.
Listen, you have to stay away from people like Lalo.
You don't see Lalo. I see Lalo. I'm in the game. You're not in the game.
But he's not your client. So, please, just... keep away.

And I'm worried about you. Look, when I was out there... I didn't think I was gonna make it. I thought I was done. Dead. I was this close to giving up. And the only thing that kept me going was knowing you were here. So...
Good. Good.
Go look in the bag.
The bag. In the living room.
On the chair. The grey bag...
You see it?
That's what it's all about.
Cereal... probably safest thing for my stomach.
I’ll get it--
You going in late?
Kim. I can take care of myself.
Ah... God, I'm sorry. Shit. I don't think... my stomach's ready for this.
You're sure you don't need to go into the office?
That sounds... real good, actually.
Saul Goodman, speedy justice for you. I'm sorry. Today's just... it's just impossible today. I can't help you. That’s right.
I'm sorry, they're doing what? Hold on. Give me forty-five minutes, I'll meet you down there.
You tell them I’m on my way.
It’s a client. He’s in big trouble. They're trying to kill his plea deal because his buddy was carrying weed.
He’s scared out of his mind. I’m not gonna feel right leaving him hanging.
No judgments.
Okay. You’re right. Something happened. When I was out there...
When I was in the desert, I... I had to drink pee. Okay? I didn't have any water, so to survive I drank my own pee. A lot. Okay? That's it, so... I'll recover. But we never need to mention it again.
I gotta get ready and get going.
It's me. I need to talk to you.
Yeah. You said... you said this goes away. What was the time frame on that?
But for me. When do you think it will be over for me?
So... what happened out there? It doesn't bother you?
What about Fred? The kid at Travel Wire. Was he in the game?
Yeah. Lalo. Lalo killed that guy. For what? He killed that guy and we're helping him. All this, all this shit to help him get out of jail and get away.
Wait a minute. What does that mean? “Not the end of the story.” Are you saying..? Are you saying what I think you’re saying? Is something gonna happen to Lalo?
Jesus. Jesus, what am I involved with? What are you saying’s gonna happen--?
I can't believe... there's a billion people on this planet, and the only person I have to talk to about this is you?
Hmm? Yeah. W-What time is it?
No. I’m up.
I’m fine. I think I just need food. I haven’t really eaten since... before everything.
Kim. I’m really okay.
Yeah. You seem... worried, maybe?
What kind of news?
Oh. So good news?
Great. So lay it on me.
Hold on, what? What happened? Did somebody say something about what we did? Was it Rich?
It felt right? How? Why?!
You're just going to throw it away? You busted your ass for all of it!
C’mon, look, it's... it’s been a rough few days. Just... wait on the decision. Call Rich and tell him you're thinking it over--
Okay, "pro bono" is wonderful and all, but "pro bono" means no money. What’s the plan here?
Look, leaving Schweikart, I get it. Bunch of stuffed shirts. But Mesa Verde? It's like leaving the Yankees to go play amateur ring toss.
Listen. This is a bad idea.
Look, we all make choices. And those choices put us on a road. And the road... it's got good choices and bad choices. And this is the bad choice road.
Bad choices lead to bad roads that lead to bad places.
What I did is completely different!
I was leaving failure for success--
I'm just giving you a reality check. This is too far, too fast.
Yeah?
So you can hear? Hear what?
Lalo. Hi. Thought you'd be down south... enjoying freedom.
Um, can I get you a drink? There’s beer in the fridge, I think...
Or maybe you’re not staying that long?
Hey, you... I’m sorry. You shouldn't do that. It... upsets the fish.
Lalo, if... you wanna talk, we can talk. Kim was just stepping out, so we can just--
Okay.
What happened.
You mean, what I told you already?

Okay, ah... Well. I picked up the money. From your cousins. Right where you told me. Driving back, my car crapped out, six or seven miles down that road. I didn’t have cell service, so I walked. North. Through the night. I slept, but kept going the next day until I finally found a truck stop. Cleaned up in the bathroom, bought new clothes and called a cab. Delivered the money. They took a few hours to count it and then... then I saw you.
What?

Fine, sure. I, uh, I picked up the money from those two fine... gentlemen. My car broke down. I didn't have phone service. I was afraid to hitchhike with the money, so I walked. Ran out of water, drank my own pee. You want more details, there ya go. Made it to a truck stop, called a taxi. The driver took me right to the courthouse. I paid the bail, got you out. I-I don't understand what you're after..?
I picked up two big bags of money. Seven million dollars. The heavy, heavy bags you hired me to get.
I put them in the trunk of my car. Drove maybe ten minutes, the engine went. I couldn’t fix it. Overheated or something. So...

I walked. I walked and walked, north. Through the desert. Walked, walked, walked. Got to the truck stop and went in the bathroom. Stuck my head under the faucet, bought a giant pack of energy drinks. Called a taxi and waited.
Look, if there's a problem, just let her out of here, she doesn't have to be here, she didn't do anything. It's me, it's all me.
Whatever you think I did, I don't know. Something's going on here, so please, just...
Okay? I--
I, what?
I don't think so.
Lalo, I... don't know what you want. You want the money back? Just take it. It's in the other room.
I told you what happened.
Look, okay, I--

lines.dialogue: Hey, I found a phone!

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - MUD ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Looks like it’s from 1967, but I think it’ll work...

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yeah, we know. We won’t. No prob. When you’re done there, could you grab a couple more lamps from the garage? Thanks.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - DAY
lines.dialogue: All right, we got a phone. Front yard’s half-mowed -- looking good.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - DINING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: ... Most of the sockets and stuff look a-ok, but I’m gonna check one more time. Make sure I didn’t miss any. Think we’re getting there!

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - DINING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: I think... off.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - DINING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Chuck... You sure this is the right way to go? I mean, the bigger the lie, the harder it’s gonna be to dig out.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - DINING ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: ... Chuck?

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - DINING ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Hey, what’s with the candles? Why’re you sitting in the dark?

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - DINING ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Jeez. Should we, I dunno, get out of here? Go to a restaurant? We could hit Seasons! Your treat.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - DINING ROOM - LATER
lines.dialogue: Cheers to the Galloping Gourmet!

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - DINING ROOM - LATER
lines.dialogue: Come on. The dishes are the least I can do. Gimme that.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Chuck --?

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Rebecca... Rebecca...

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Rebecca.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Chuck... tell her!

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Okay, gimme one minute and we can --

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Please, let me.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: You have to do something. You can’t just let her walk outta here! Tell her what’s going on.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: She’ll understand! You think it's better she thinks you're a raging prick than she knows the truth??

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Okay. You won’t tell her, then I’ll tell her.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK’S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Chuck, please --

lines.scene: INT. VETERINARIAN’S OFFICE - EXAM ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: “Her?”

lines.scene: INT. VETERINARIAN’S OFFICE - EXAM ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Oh yeah. Now that I look, I can see the lipstick.

lines.scene: INT. VETERINARIAN’S OFFICE - EXAM ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: All right already, Jacques Cousteau! Point made.

lines.scene: INT. VETERINARIAN’S OFFICE - EXAM ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yeah, look, I need someone with a light touch. I’m not talking some kid who’s taking a five-finger discount on string cheese at the local Stop ‘N’ Shop -- I’m talking highly skilled, high end, discreet. A pro.

lines.scene: INT. VETERINARIAN’S OFFICE - EXAM ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Don’t think so.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - LATER
lines.dialogue: What are you still doing here?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - LATER
lines.dialogue: How delayed?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - LATER
lines.dialogue: Shit. Okay. Keep me posted.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - LATER
lines.dialogue: Begging your pardon, but the defense would like a moment to review first. If we could?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - LATER
lines.dialogue: Thank you, Mr. Chairman.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - LATER
lines.dialogue: Stalling.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HALLWAY - DAY
lines.dialogue: ... I sure as shit wouldn’t be telling you otherwise. But, yes. It’s the truth.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HALLWAY - DAY
lines.dialogue: I did it for Kim! She worked her butt off to get Mesa Verde..!

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: ... She earned it, and she needs it. I did it to help her, but I -- I honestly didn’t think it would hurt you so bad.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: I thought you’d just say, “Oh crap, I made a mistake,” and go on with your life, like a normal person. But, oh no! Wishful thinking..!

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: I’m gonna go call Howard.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: I guess. But you feel better, right? Besides, it’s your word against mine.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - CONTINUOUS
lines.dialogue: I left it in my car.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HALLWAY - DAY
lines.dialogue: What did you expect?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HALLWAY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yep.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Y’know, there’s been a lot of fuss about it, but you and I, we’ve never really talked about this tape you made.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Fair enough. I was in the wrong there. But still. I’d like to see if I can follow your story about why and how you recorded it.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: No. That’s me on the tape.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: But I still have questions. Like, the recorder -- man, that must’ve hurt like hell for you to touch.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Where did you even hide it? It sounds pretty clear. It wasn’t in the couch cushions, was it?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Wow. No chance I'd see that! Not with the state your place was in. Isn't that right?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Could you set the scene for the Disciplinary Committee? Tell us what your house looked like when the recording was made.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: The circumstances of the recording are materially relevant. How can you understand what the tape really means if you don’t know what was going on when it was made?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: What do they look like?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: So shiny insulation and space blankets -- all over the walls and ceiling. It was like being inside a disco ball.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: I’m impressed by how much work went into entrapping me. You went all out.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: How’d you know it would work?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: I mean, how’d you know your ‘provocation’ would work? Why would you think a bunch of shiny plastic would make me say anything?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Isn’t it because you knew that was precisely the thing that would worry me so much I’d say anything to talk you down?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Withdrawn.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Let’s get back to your house, every surface covered in tin foil. Nothing crazy about that.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Really? You think your house is normal? Can I call your attention to Exhibit Twelve..? That’s your house, isn’t it?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Huh... I mean, I see pulled wires. Camp stoves. Lanterns on top of newspapers... Would you say those are "normal?"

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Did the doctor who granted me a Guardianship for you think this is a “physical condition?”

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: The State Bar opened the door to this on direct when the witness talked about his supposed “play- acting.” Allowing me to follow up on cross is only reasonable.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Potato, po-tah-to! Look, it comes down to this: in order for you to know what I was thinking, you need to see Chuck through my eyes. You need to know if I believed that tape was evidence. And I say the only thing it’s evidence of is the fact my brother hates me. He claims he lied to get me to tell the truth. I'm telling you I lied to make my brother feel better. Which of us you believe depends on how we all understand the mind of Charles McGill.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Thank you, Mr. Chairman.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Can we go back a little further, Chuck? I’d like to talk about when your symptoms first appeared. It was shortly after you were divorced, is that correct?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Do you think the stress of the divorce might’ve brought on your illness?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: In fact, your ex-wife is present here today, is she not? When was the last time you saw her?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yes. I do. Earlier, you talked about some other diseases. Physical conditions, you said. Okay. So let’s say you had, I dunno... lung cancer. Would you have told Rebecca then?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: So... how is this different? COMMITTEE MEMBER #2 Mr. McGill. Move it along.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: You know what, you don’t need to answer that. Let’s get down to brass tacks. I want to be very, very specific here. This illness, what does it feel like? You mentioned it’s painful.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Sounds horrible. Does it hurt right now?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: The lights, the microphones. When they’re off you don’t feel them?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Sorry about the exit signs. Guess they couldn't kill those for you.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Whoa! Inverse-square! I’m no physicist. Could you dumb that down a shade for me?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Got it, got it. So if I had a small battery, from a watch or something -- if I got it close enough to you, near your skin maybe, you’d know?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Can you feel more current from any particular direction right now? Anything coming through the wall back there? Or over there? What about through the floor? Can you tell us where the nearest source is?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Uh... yes. I do, in fact.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: My cellphone. At this distance, you should feel it, shouldn’t you? And you don’t!

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yep. You got me, Chuck. Dead to rights. I took the battery out.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: I don’t know, Chuck.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Could you reach into your breast pocket? Tell me what’s there.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Could you tell the court what that was?

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Do you recognize that man in the back? His name is Huell Babineaux - - he’s on our witness list. You remember, you bumped into him in the stairway. He’ll testify he planted that fully-charged battery on you over an hour and a half ago!

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: Thank you, Mr. Babineaux. An hour and forty three minutes! And you felt nothing.

lines.scene: INT. STATE BAR BUILDING - HEARING ROOM - DAY
lines.dialogue: No. Nothing further.
Get in!
We gotta reshoot! Three hundred bucks for ninety minutes! C'mon!

You're not hearing me, it's FOUR hundred dollars if you get in the car now. I’ll set your boss straight if he gives you any grief. In fact, I'll sue his ass for wrongful termination and age discrimination if he fires you!

Listen, how many chances do you get to use your craft and shine? Lose yourself inside the skin of another character and create magic that others only dream of? My advice? Don't live with the regret. Carpe diem, man!
There ya go! That’s the spirit that takes people places. Just buckle up, okay? I don’t wanna lose you through the windshield.
What are you doing teaching a class? I told you, we’ve got zero time...
What do you mean “discuss your fee?” Your fee is your fee...
Five hundred? I gave you one hundred last week for the same job.
Fine! Five hundred! Jesus.
Yeah, pinky, all the fingers, anything. Just... don’t tell the others.
The best ass reaming.
We’re just gonna shoot over there, trees in the background, throw it all way out-of-focus. That work?
How’s our boy looking?
I like it, that’s good--
Would you leave her alone and go set up whatever it is you need to set up?
No, it's taken care of.
Truer words were never spoken. Let’s get it in gear, people, we’re on a deadline!
Thank God...
You’re sure? I mean absolutely sure?
Of course, but I can do it. I was around your cast almost as much as you were. Here, gimme the bag. You get back on the road, bust the speed limit, you can still make the lunch.
Left arm.
Your character has a broken arm now. LENNY CAMERA GUY JIMMY SOUND GUY LENNY CAMERA GUY KIM SOUND GUY JIMMY CAMERA GUY LENNY SOUND GUY DRAMA GIRL CAMERA GUY

Your motivation is still exactly the same. A covert mission receiving an envelope of great importance, but you don’t want anyone to know what you’re doing, so you act casual, but knowing. JJIIMMMMYY ((CCOONNTT''DD)) There’s intrigue, mystery, conspiracy... Probably best just to look sleepy. Jesus, Mary and Joseph, how we doing, everyone?
It’s a park in Albuquerque, not the African bush, c’mon...
What?
Good, got it, go--
What are we looking at?
Okay, this one, this one, this one and... this one?
Don’t worry about it. You’re “need- to-know” on this one.
Oh God oh God oh God...
Y'know... we don't have to answer it.
Let me. Just in case Max Schmeling comes in swinging.
Yeah. Sure.
A gift? What's the occasion?
Won. What'd I win?
We're good.
Burn you to the ground? Okay. Come on. You're gonna be fine, Howard. You always land on your feet.
Okay, Howard. We're gonna call you a cab. You're too tight to drive, so let’s just...
Enough, Howard.
How?
No!
Yeah... it's me. I'm okay.
It's hard to explain... I’m coming home. Today.
Yes. I'm coming back to you. I swear...
You know... You and me... We're sitting on seven million bucks here. Literally.
I say we split it fifty-fifty and take off.
It could be.
Them? Forget about them.
The first thing we do, we put six million bucks into building a time machine. Those people you're worried about? They're never gonna find us.
Where do you go first? Looking at you, I'm gonna say you're a history buff. The Civil War..? Ancient Rome..?
Why?
Easy. May 10, 1965. The day Warren Buffett took over Berkshire Hathaway. There'd still be a million left over from building the time machine, I'd take my half and put it straight into Berkshire.
I'd pop back here and I'd be... A billionaire. More. Is there such a thing as a trillionaire?
What else?
I'm rested.

lines.scene: INT. GENE'S APARTMENT - DAY
lines.dialogue: "Hoover Max Extract Pressure-Pro, model sixty."

lines.scene: INT. GENE'S APARTMENT - DAY
lines.dialogue: Krista? Hi, it's Gene... Sorry I wasn't in this morning, did you open up okay? I'm fine -- listen, can you do me a favor? The week's rotation needs to be posted by three -- do you think you can take care of that?

lines.scene: INT. GENE'S APARTMENT - DAY
lines.dialogue: Great. Uh, one more thing, can you call the main office? GGEENNEE ((CCOONNTT''DD)) The number’s on the bulletin board, let them know you're going to need a new manager... No. Looks like I won’t... Yeah, it is kind of last minute...

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: That's how they get you? That's how? That's how? Jesus! What were you thinking? GENE What -- GENE Were -- GENE You --

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: THINKING..!

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Shit! SAUL Hey! Another phone call! I need another phone call!

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Keep up, Bill. You've hit the jackpot.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: This puts you on the map, amigo. Here's what you're gonna do. You're gonna grab a flight to Omaha, Nebraska, ASAP. There's nothing direct, you'll have to connect through Houston.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: You are. Listen! You hear that?

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Bang, bang! It's opportunity knocking! Get off your ass and open the door! On your way to the airport, you gotta make some calls. Find out which Assistant US Attorney’s catching the case -- my money's on George Castellano. Whoever it is, tell 'em we're ready to talk. I wanna get on this before they extradite me to New Mexico. All hands on deck here in Omaha, no later than five o'clock tomorrow.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: "Willing?" Bill, this is a career- maker. Get real, you’re doing this.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Where do I see this ending? With me on top. Like always.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Agent Schrader's widow is back there. Why don't you invite her in?

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Don't you owe her that?

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Bill, she’s already here. All parties agree. It’s fine.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Mrs. Schrader, the loss you've suffered... It's... unspeakable. I met your husband a few times. He was very good at his job. He was a man who stood by his word. A straight shooter. You and he are victims. SSAAUULL ((CCOONNTT''DD)) And so am I.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Two years ago a man came into my office. He told me his name was Mayhew. He wanted one of my clients to lie under oath. He offered me money. I refused. Any lawyer would.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: That night, as I was leaving my office, men attacked me. They shoved a bag over my head, hogtied me and drove me out to the desert. When they took that hood off, I was on my knees in front of an open grave. A gun was pointed at my head. That was my introduction to Walter White.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Since that night, there hasn’t been a minute that I wasn’t afraid. You’re right. I did help him. But only because I knew what he’d do if I refused. Over and over, I thought about going to the police, I even thought about going to Agent Schrader. But I knew that Walter White would kill me, no matter where I was.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: And I was right. October fourth, two thousand nine. Look it up. They murdered ten men in three prisons in the space of two minutes. Knifed. Throats slashed. A man was burned alive. SSAAUULL ((CCOONNTT''DD)) They killed one of my colleagues, an attorney I knew very well. Daniel Wachsburger. He was cooperating with the DEA. The news said Danny was stabbed forty-eight times.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: So when it all blew up... I ran. Not from the police. From them. Walter White might be dead, but Jesse Pinkman and the rest? They're still out there, somewhere.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Mrs. Schrader, you're looking at a man who's lost everything. My profession. My freedom. My family. It's all gone. I have nobody. I have... nothing. CASTELLANO And you think jurors are gonna buy that? SAUL One. That's all I need. Just one. SAUL Bill Oakley tells me you’ve never lost a case, is that right?

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Quite a record. You gotta be proud of that. Still... Juries. You never can tell. Always a roll of the dice. I'm hoping there's a little wiggle room here.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Seven and a half years.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: "Nineteen. Term to be served at FCI Butner Low, North Carolina. Wing D."

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: That’s FCI Butner Low. Only federal institution with a golf program. It was good enough for Bernie Madoff...

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: You think I'm leaving it up to you? I know how you guys work, I give you half a chance, you'll throw me into gen pop in some hellhole. I visited a client in ADX Montrose once. "Alcatraz of the Rockies." Whoa. No way, my friend. Dealbreaker.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: You got that? "Blue Bell Mint Chocolate Chip." No substitutions.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Hold on. There's a way to oil everybody's locks.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: I've got a sweetener. Nothing to do with anything we've talked about. New arena. And it's primo.

lines.scene: INT. LOCAL PRECINCT - HOLDING CELL - DAY
lines.dialogue: Inside story on a previously unknown felony homicide. It concerns a prominent Albuquerque attorney who disappeared and is presumed to have killed himself --

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Am I gonna be sorry if I ask what’s going on?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: A stop to what?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: The click?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: The thermocouple is corroded. Got it. We couldn't just pull the plug?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Yeah. That click, you know, it's pretty quiet. Most people could sleep through something like that.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Yeah. “Most people.” Got it. SAUL You know... I haven’t shared a room with another guy since I was twelve. SAUL So, I’ve got a question for you. You’re a scientist, I’ve always wondered -- if people could fly, would you be able to fly as high as a jet? Or would it be too cold up there?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: No?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: What would you do with a time machine?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Yeah, a time machine. It can take you anywhere, forward, back -- you can go see the dinosaurs, kill Hitler, date Cleopatra -- okay, possibly the language barrier’d be a problem there -- but you get the idea. What're you gonna do?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: What about wormholes? I saw something on NOVA and Alan Alda seemed to think --

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I'm just saying, as a thought experiment...

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: ... there’s gotta be something you’d go back and change. If you could.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: All right. Then... Regrets.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: You started a company. It's still around?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: And it's successful?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Why did you never tell me this!? We could have done something with this! Wrongful termination... intellectual property theft... patent fraud! I coulda gotten my teeth into this!

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Yeah. Sure.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Oh, yeah...

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: When I first went out on my own, as a solo practitioner, I was looking for an office. I had two choices. There was a room over a copy shop -- two hundred twenty-five a month. And there was the back of a nail salon. A hundred seventy-five. Fifty bucks is fifty bucks, right? I went with the nail salon. Giant mistake. You know the stuff they use on nail polish..?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Acetone. That stuff, the smell gets up your nose and into the back of your throat and just stays there. I was breathing acetone all day, every day. For years. Still can't smell right.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Wait, I got another. I was twenty, twenty-two, I pulled a slip and fall outside Marshall Field's. SSAAUULL ((CCOONNTT''DD)) I was young and stupid and I wanted to show off, you know? So I took the ice as fast as I could -- I biffed it so hard that when I went down I heard this crack! And it wasn’t the ice -- it was me, I actually hurt myself! My knees’ve never been the same.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Yeah. That’s how I put myself through bartending school.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Ssst! Bill!

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: He's my lawyer.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Hold on. Nothing I say in front of you is privileged, right?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: And if I talk to my attorney here, and we happen to let something slip that'd help the government's case, you could pass it on to the prosecution. Totally clean.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: With that in mind, you're sure we can't say a few words?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: So she confessed. What's the DA gonna do with it?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Okay.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Then what?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: No.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: And is she? Suing?

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Bill! Hold up.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: You're gonna love this. The Hamlin thing? Government doesn't know the half of it.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Soon as we land, let the other side know I've got more to trade. I just remembered something that'll make their toes curl.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: It involves her.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: You don't understand, Bill. It's really good ice cream.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Showtime.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: That night, as I was leaving my office, men attacked me. They shoved a bag over my head, hogtied me and drove me out to the desert. When they took the hood off, I was on my knees in front of an open grave. A gun was pointed at my head. That was my introduction to Walter White. I was terrified.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: ... But not for long. Because that night I saw opportunity. A shot at the big money. I grabbed it and held on tight. For the next sixteen months, my every waking moment was spent building Walter White's drug empire --

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Your Honor, I believe I owe the court the whole truth.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: No offense, your Honor, but I'm pretty sure I know the law here better than you do.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: We don't need a recess.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I do.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Yes.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: No, your Honor.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: No.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Oh, yeah. By the way, I lied to the government about Kim Wexler. I sold them a load of b.s. about her involvement in Howard Hamlin's death. I lied because I wanted to get her to come here today. I want her to hear this.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: It's true, I wasn't present when meth was cooked. I wasn't there when it was sold, I didn't witness the murders. But I knew damn well it was happening. I was more than a willing participant, I was indispensable. SSAAUULL ((CCOONNTT''DD)) I kept Walter White out of jail, I laundered his money, I lied for him, I conspired with him... And I made millions.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: If he hadn't walked into my office that day, Walter White would have been dead or behind bars within a month. And Agent Schrader, Agent Gomez and... a lot of other people would still be alive.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: The truth is... Walter White couldn't have done it without me.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: You got that? OAKLEY Your Honor, we move to strike Mr. Goodman's comments. JUDGE SMALL On what grounds? OAKLEY Speculation. JUDGE SMALL Speculation? He's testifying to his own actions.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Hold on, I've got more --

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Please, your Honor. Please.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: What happened to Howard Hamlin... that was... It was... I can't even...

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: After that, Kim had the guts to start over and I... Well, she left town but I'm the one who ran away.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: And Chuck... My brother Charles McGill, some of you knew him.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: He was an incredible lawyer, the most brilliant guy I've ever known. But he was... limited. I tried. I should have tried harder. I could have. Instead...

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Shut up, Bill. Just let me get through this.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Instead, when I saw a chance to hurt him, I took it. I got his malpractice insurance canceled. I took away the one thing he lived for. The law. After that, he killed himself. It didn't have to go that way. And I live with that.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Kim Wexler was a lawyer for all the right reasons. I hope she goes back to the law. She can still do some good.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Yeah, it was.

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: The name's McGill, your Honor. Jimmy McGill. OAKLEY NOORYANI sentencing recommendation --

lines.scene: INT. BEST QUALITY VACUUM CLEANER - HIDDEN SAFE ROOM - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Yeah, I did -- Crap!

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: My car conked out on I-40. I almost got creamed by a cement truck.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I got it, I got it.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: They had the Fuji apples you like so I got a half dozen. And the newsstand on Central says they might start getting the Financial Times, so there's that.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: What?

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I'm doing it.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Why? Because I'm your brother. Duh. You'd do the same for me.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Talk about what?

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: You want to talk about my clients? You want to talk about the grandma who was soliciting inside a Christian Science Reading Room? You want to talk about the kid who broke into a liquor store, drank five bottles of crème de menthe and passed out behind the counter?

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Or maybe you just wanna tell me everything I'm doing wrong.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: You can hope.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I'll take a rain check on the heart- to-heart. One of my "deserving" clients just got picked up waving the weenie outside a Hobby Lobby.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: This one's on me.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Oh, yeah? When have you ever "changed your path?"

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: Nothing comes to mind? Keep thinking it over, okay?

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: See ya, Chuck.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: McGill.

lines.scene: INT. CHUCK'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT
lines.dialogue: I'm McGill.

lines.scene: INT. FEDERAL PRISON - BAKERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Hi.

lines.scene: INT. FEDERAL PRISON - BAKERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: How'd you..?

lines.scene: INT. FEDERAL PRISON - BAKERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Yeah. I did.

lines.scene: INT. FEDERAL PRISON - BAKERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: Eighty-six.

lines.scene: INT. FEDERAL PRISON - BAKERY - DAY
lines.dialogue: But with good behavior... who knows?
